item.title: Australia’s Victoria State Approves $700 Million Gas Project
item.description: Australia’s Victoria state has approved the production license for a A$1 billion ($700 million) natural gas project to help avoid a forecast gas shortage.

item.title: Treasuries Surge as Worldwide Worries Spark Rush to Safety
item.description: Treasuries rallied for their best day in more than two years, surging across the board as a deepening rout in AI-related shares, market turmoil in France and fresh Mideast tensions all combined to make US government debt the investment of choice for anxious traders.

item.title: Australian Growth Likely Slower Than Expected, Chalmers Says
item.description: Australia’s growth will likely be slower than the 1.75% forecast in May’s budget, Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers said Friday, as a series of rate hikes and rising inflation start to bite on the economy.

item.title: What a 35-Hour Train Ride Reveals About Vietnam’s Future
item.description: Vietnam is betting big on a $65 billion high-speed railway linking Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Construction is set to start in late 2027 and take at least a decade to complete. The line could cut the roughly 35-hour journey to just six hours. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New York City Bans Horse-Drawn Carriages After Decade-Long Battle
item.description: New York’s City Council voted to ban horse-drawn carriages, ending a Central Park tourist staple dating to the 19th century after years of debate over the horses’ place on city streets. Bloomberg's Laura Nahmias explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
